network.tdh.how.pageTitle: How TDH is calculated, step by step | Network
network.tdh.how.metadataDescription: Copies, whole days, edition rates, boosts and consolidations, with worked examples you can change.
network.tdh.how.title: How TDH is calculated
network.tdh.how.lede: This page follows one day’s calculation in the order the computer does it. It describes TDH-v1 as specification P26 writes it. P26 is still a proposal; by the owner’s decisions, 6529.io computes it from the cutover, about October 23, 2026. Step 14 lists what changes from today.
network.tdh.how.basis: Every number on this page is computed in your browser by a TypeScript port of the TDH-v1 arithmetic, tested against values the Python reference prints, rechecked at P26 f840096, its latest change. The computation of record is 6529.io’s until the cutover, and the validators’ Rust core from then on. Rates, boosts and the full example use the network of the October 11, 2026 cycle, the day the specification was replayed against 6529.io record by record: the largest edition was FirstGM’s 3,941, 559 Memes were eligible in 17 seasons, and there were 101 Gradients and 1,000 NextGen tokens. The date examples use the cycle of October 15, 2026 (20,741).
network.tdh.how.pipeline.title: The calculation, step by step
network.tdh.how.pipeline.desc: The fourteen steps of this page in order, each linking to its section: the calculation runs from step 1, the snapshot, to step 13, the network total; step 12 is a worked example and step 14 what changes at the cutover.
network.tdh.how.pipeline.legendResult: Where the calculation ends: the network total
network.tdh.how.pipeline.legendAside: Beside the calculation: a worked example, and what changes at the cutover
network.tdh.how.s1.title: One snapshot a day
network.tdh.how.s1.body: TDH is computed once a day. Day N closes at 00:00 UTC, and the snapshot is the last Ethereum block before that moment. Ethereum offers a slot every 12 seconds and 23:59:59 is always one of them, so the snapshot block is normally stamped 23:59:59; if that slot was empty, it is the block before.
network.tdh.how.s1.finality: The calculation waits until Ethereum has finalized the next block, normally a quarter of an hour or so after midnight, so that no reorganisation can change the snapshot.
network.tdh.how.s1.example: The cycle of October 15, 2026 is cycle {cycle}, the number of days since January 1, 1970. Its boundary is 00:00:00 UTC, Unix time {boundary}. With the snapshot block stamped 23:59:59 on October 14, ages are measured to {snapshot}.
network.tdh.how.s2.title: Whole days
network.tdh.how.s2.body: A copy’s age is the number of whole days between when you got it and the snapshot’s time. Partial days do not count.
network.tdh.how.s2.tableCaption: Whole days for three acquisition times
network.tdh.how.s2.reference: 6529.io’s backend measures ages to the snapshot block’s time, not to midnight, and TDH-v1 keeps that (DEV-17).
network.tdh.how.s3.title: Which cards count
network.tdh.how.s3.body: The Memes, Gradients and NextGen count. A Meme or a Gradient counts once its first mint is at least one full day old; a NextGen token counts once minted. The clock starts at the very first mint, including the zero-copy mint by which a Manifold claim creates a card. Meme Lab, received xTDH, prices, REP and $6529 balances are not inputs.
network.tdh.how.s4.title: Every copy has a timestamp
network.tdh.how.s4.body: For each card, each wallet keeps a list of acquisition times, one per copy. A copy received from someone else is stamped with the time of the transfer. When you send copies, they leave from the end of the list, which is normally your most recent purchase, so you keep your oldest copies: last in, first out.
network.tdh.how.s4.example: Wallet A bought three copies of a card 300, 200 and 100 days before the snapshot, and sold one 50 days before it.
network.tdh.how.s4.tableCaption: Last in, first out after one sale
network.tdh.how.s4.burns: Minting debits nobody. Sending a copy to the zero address or to 0x…dead is a burn: the copy stops counting for its holder, and the card’s edition size does not shrink.
network.tdh.how.s4.diagramTitle: Wallet A’s stack at the sale and at the snapshot
network.tdh.how.s4.diagramDesc: At the sale, 50 days before the snapshot, Wallet A’s copies are 250, 150 and 50 days old, oldest at the bottom. The sale takes the top copy, the newest, and the buyer’s stack starts it at 0 days. At the snapshot Wallet A’s two copies are 300 and 200 days old, and the buyer’s copy is 50 days old.
network.tdh.how.s5.title: Ownership is read between transactions
network.tdh.how.s5.body: Ethereum only shows who owns what between transactions, so TDH looks at each transaction as a whole. Within one transaction, each wallet’s movements of each card are netted, and only the net change counts. A copy that leaves a wallet and comes back inside one transaction never left. A to B to C inside one transaction counts as A to C. Movements in different transactions keep their order, even inside one block.
network.tdh.how.s5.example: Wallet A has held a copy for 300 days. Twenty days before the snapshot, one transaction sends it out and brings it back.
network.tdh.how.s5.tableCaption: A round trip inside one transaction
network.tdh.how.s5.inOrder: Every movement in order, without netting
network.tdh.how.s5.measured: On October 14 and 15, 2026, before netting, this was the only kind of difference between the new computation and 6529.io: two collectors each day, each with a token sent out and back in one transaction. With netting, every collector and wallet agrees on both days.
network.tdh.how.s5.diagramDesc: Inside one transaction, a copy moves from Wallet A to Wallet C and back from Wallet C to Wallet A. Netted, Wallet A’s change is zero and the copy keeps its age.
network.tdh.how.s6.title: Edition sizes
network.tdh.how.s6.body: A card’s edition is the number of copies minted. Burns do not reduce it. FirstGM is the one adjusted card: 6,529 minted, minus 2,588 copies from its recorded burn, gives 3,941.
network.tdh.how.s6.floor: A Meme with fewer than 300 copies minted counts at least at its claim’s mint limit, capped at 310: the size its final top-up airdrop brings it to. With no claim, or a limit below the minted count, the minted count is used. From 300 copies on, the minted count is the edition.
network.tdh.how.s6.cycle: On the 2026-10-11 cycle only Meme 559 was below 300 copies (149 minted); Memes 206, 215 and 311 keep 309, 309 and 303 copies although their claims allow more.
network.tdh.how.s7.title: Rates
network.tdh.how.s7.body: The largest edition among eligible Memes sets the scale: H = 3,941. Each card’s rate is H divided by its edition, rounded to cents. A Gradient’s rate uses the number of Gradients and never falls below 1.00; a NextGen token’s uses the size of its collection.
network.tdh.how.s7.tie: Rounding detail: at an exact half cent, the computer’s binary arithmetic decides, as 6529.io’s backend does. A 200-copy edition would get 19.70, not 19.71.
network.tdh.how.s7.curveDesc: The rate falls as the edition grows: 3,941 divided by the edition, on a logarithmic edition axis from 100 to 4,000. Labelled points: Gradients at 101 (39.02), a 300-copy and a 310-copy Meme together (13.14 and 12.71), NextGen at 1,000 (3.94) and FirstGM at 3,941 (1.00). Below 300 copies minted, a Meme whose claim allows 310 or more is counted at 310.
network.tdh.how.s7.floorBand: Below 300 minted, claim of 310 or more: counted as 310
network.tdh.how.s8.title: Base TDH per card
network.tdh.how.s8.body: Add up the whole days of your copies of a card, multiply by its rate, and round to a whole number. A copy with zero whole days adds nothing yet.
network.tdh.how.s8.example: One copy of a 310-copy Meme held 100 days: 100 × 12.71 = {base}.
network.tdh.how.s8.perWallet: Rounding happens per wallet, per card. If two wallets of one collector each hold that card for one day, each rounds 12.71 to {one}, so the collector has {two}, not {merged}.
network.tdh.how.s9.title: The boost
network.tdh.how.s9.body: One multiplier applies to everything a collector holds. It starts at 1.00 and grows with complete sets, complete seasons and Gradients. A copy counts for the boost from the moment you hold it, even before it has a whole day.
network.tdh.how.s9.seasons: Complete seasons: +0.05 for each season you hold completely, for seasons 1 to 20, except the current season, which starts paying once a later season begins.
network.tdh.how.s9.partial: Season 1, partly: without the whole season, Memes 1, 2 and 3 (Genesis) add +0.01 and Meme 4 (Nakamoto) adds +0.01.
network.tdh.how.s9.fullSet: A full set of every eligible Meme gives every season bonus at once (+0.80 on the October 11 cycle, 16 seasons × 0.05), and each further full set adds a smaller bonus: +0.05, then about +0.033, +0.021 and so on, approaching +0.144 in total.
network.tdh.how.s9.tableIntro: Examples on the 2026-10-11 cycle (17 seasons, so seasons 1 to 16 pay):
network.tdh.how.s9.ex.season2GenesisNaka: All of Season 2, Genesis and Nakamoto
network.tdh.how.s9.ex.currentSeasonOnly: All of Season 17, the current season, only
network.tdh.how.s9.ex.allButNewest: Every Meme except the newest one
network.tdh.how.s9.ex.highest: 8 or more full sets and 5 Gradients, the highest on that cycle
network.tdh.how.s9.newest: “Every Meme except the newest” equals a full set on that day because the missing card is in the current season, which pays nothing yet, while seasons 1 to 16 are complete. With 17 seasons listed, the highest boost is 2.04, reached with 8 full sets and 5 Gradients; more sets still add to the extra-set bonus, up to 33 sets, but no longer change the rounded boost. The schedule pays seasons up to 20, so a higher boost needs new seasons added to the season list. The boost rounds to cents, and its rounding never meets a tie.
network.tdh.how.s10.title: Consolidating wallets
network.tdh.how.s10.body: A collector can make several wallets count as one identity. Each wallet registers the other in the delegation contract under the consolidation use case (999), for The Memes or for all collections. One direction is pending; both directions confirm the link. Either wallet can revoke it.
network.tdh.how.s10.limit: Under rule version tdh-v1.0 an identity holds up to three wallets, and every pair of them must be confirmed. Groups are formed newest confirmed link first.
network.tdh.how.s10.fourth: Four wallets that all confirm each other form one identity of three, starting from the newest link, and the fourth counts as an identity of its own (P26 §6.3). 6529.io’s consolidation guide allows a fourth wallet for links registered after its start date, so unless the rule is amended before the cutover, about October 23, 2026, such a group splits that way at the cutover: the fourth wallet’s cards no longer add to the others’ sets or boost.
network.tdh.how.s10.change1: Your holdings add up across wallets, card by card.
network.tdh.how.s10.change2: The boost is computed on the combined holdings, so a set split across wallets counts.
network.tdh.how.s10.change3: Moving a copy between your own wallets keeps its age. Example: a copy held 300 days in Wallet A and moved to Wallet B 10 days ago counts 300 days if A and B are consolidated, and 10 if they are not.
network.tdh.how.s10.change4: The grouping at the snapshot applies to the whole history, including moves made before the wallets were consolidated, as 6529.io’s backend does today. It can also take age away: if the wallets later separate, or a newer link regroups them, a copy that carried age inside the identity is stamped again at its transfer time on the next cycle.
network.tdh.how.s10.delegation: Delegation is not consolidation. Delegations for other uses, their expiry, their token scope and their updates do not change TDH.
network.tdh.how.s10.guide: Set one up with the consolidation guide
network.tdh.how.s10.graphTitle: Three link patterns and the identities they form
network.tdh.how.s10.graphDesc: Wallets are circles; confirmed links are solid lines; each identity is outlined. First: A, B and C all linked form one identity. Second: without the A–C link, the newest link B–C forms an identity and A stays alone. Third: the newest link C–D forms an identity first, then A and B.
network.tdh.how.s11.title: Final TDH
network.tdh.how.s11.body: For each card, multiply its base by the boost and round to a whole number; your TDH is the sum.
network.tdh.how.s11.tie: Rounding detail: when the product ends in exactly .5, binary arithmetic decides, as on 6529.io: 25 × 1.14 = 28.5 gives {tie}. On the 2026-10-11 cycle 82 card values rounded down this way; exact decimal rounding would have added 82 TDH in total.
network.tdh.how.s12.title: A full example: one collector, two wallets
network.tdh.how.s12.body: Wallet A and Wallet B belong to one collector and are consolidated. The snapshot is at 23:59:59 UTC.
network.tdh.how.s12.boostNote: Boost: two Gradients, so 1.04 for the identity. Each wallet alone holds one Gradient, so 1.02.
network.tdh.how.s12.result.identity: As one identity: {total} TDH. By the daily-rate formula it rises {rate} TDH a day; tomorrow it rises by {tomorrow}, because the copy bought 5 hours before the snapshot starts counting too.
network.tdh.how.s12.result.wallets: Not consolidated, the wallets would score {a} and {b}, together {total}: consolidation adds {gain} here, all from the shared boost.
network.tdh.how.s12.result.tomorrow: Tomorrow, with no other change: {total}, up {delta}. The daily rate is 1.04 × (1.00 + 1.00 + 12.71 + 39.02 + 39.02 + 3.94) = {rate} TDH a day, and the copy bought 5 hours before the snapshot starts counting.
network.tdh.how.s12.result.sell: If Wallet B sold Gradient 2 before the snapshot: {total}, down {delta}: the card’s own {own}, and the boost falls from 1.04 to 1.02 on everything else.
network.tdh.how.s13.title: Network totals
network.tdh.how.s13.body: The network total is the sum over identities. The zero address and 0x…dead keep records from burns: they are in the total, as on 6529.io, and never count as participants or toward any share of the network. On the October 11, 2026 cycle TDH-v1 gives 10,280 identities, 11,130 wallets and 2,061,888,816 TDH, the total 6529.io published. The two sink records hold 1,085,953 of it; the total without them, 2,060,802,863, is the one the validators’ signed result will carry.
network.tdh.how.s14.title: What changes when 6529.io switches to TDH-v1
network.tdh.how.s14.body: From about October 23, 2026, 6529.io shows the result of the validators’ Rust core. TDH-v1 restates today’s rule. It differs where today’s result depends on timing, database order or a failed refresh, and for groups of four wallets:
network.tdh.how.s14.item1: the snapshot block comes from the finalized chain, and the input must be complete;
network.tdh.how.s14.item2: edition floors are read at the snapshot block;
network.tdh.how.s14.item3: Gradient and NextGen rates come from on-chain counts at that block;
network.tdh.how.s14.item4: seasons come from a versioned list, not from editable metadata;
network.tdh.how.s14.item5: movements in different transactions of one block keep their on-chain order (DEV-2), while movements within one transaction are netted (D131). On October 11, and on every day compared since, TDH-v1 equals 6529.io’s values. On a day when a sale and a purchase of one card fall in different transactions of one block, it can lower a few wallets’ TDH;

network.tdh.how.s5.vectors: P26 states the rule exactly: every transaction is netted, and a sink (the zero address or 0x…dead, which are credited but never debited) is netted like any other address; sources and destinations are paired in ascending address order. Three things still read the transfers before netting: the mint facts (each card’s first mint and the counts behind its edition), the underflow test, which checks that no wallet ever sends a copy it does not hold, and the log-position checks of section 3.1. Vectors 18, 36 to 43 and 45 to 47 pin the rule, and 44 and 48 to 50 pin inputs that have no result.
network.tdh.how.boostBuilder.currentNote: Season {season} is the current season: it pays nothing until a later season begins.
network.tdh.how.s4.legend: Oldest copy at the bottom. The struck-through copy is the one sold: the newest, from the end of the list.
network.tdh.how.s10.linksNote: The numbers give each link’s order on chain, oldest first; groups form from the newest confirmed link.

network.tdh.how.s13.verify: This total is computed again and compared with 6529.io’s every day, in public.
network.tdh.how.s14.item6: consolidations count as they stand at the snapshot block. Today the backend recomputes a day’s TDH when a consolidation changes during the day; under TDH-v1 the change counts from the next cycle;
network.tdh.how.s14.item7: a fourth consolidated wallet. 6529.io’s consolidation guide allows one for links registered after its start date; under tdh-v1.0, four wallets that all confirm each other form an identity of three, from the newest link, and the fourth counts on its own (step 10). Unless the rule is amended before the cutover, such a group splits that way.
